# Email ingestion

The optional `email` profile receives **one IMAP account and folder for this
installation**. It considers all existing messages, read and unread. It publishes
only body text and selected decoded message headers; no attachment extraction, speech,
OAuth, SMTP receiver, or automatic wiki commits are included.

**The configured account/folder is the trust boundary. There is no recipient
verification or strict mode.** Without the optional recipient allowlist below,
To/Cc/Bcc and delivery headers do not filter mail. Enabling reception can archive
and delete **all eligible existing and new messages in that folder**, subject to
the optional sender and recipient allowlists and size and durability safeguards
below. Use a dedicated mailbox or reliably isolated folder.

## Before enabling destructive reception

1. Use a dedicated mailbox or restricted account with access only to the chosen
   folder. The account needs fetch, flag and targeted-delete rights.
2. Confirm TLS IMAP with certificate verification (default port 993) and password
   or app-password login. Unencrypted IMAP and STARTTLS downgrade paths are not
   supported. Some providers require OAuth and cannot use this connector.
3. Verify the selected folder contains only mail intended for this wiki, including
   its backlog. If you need recipient routing, configure and verify server-side
   delivery rules into a dedicated folder before enabling reception. The optional
   recipient allowlist is a filter, not routing or verification. Missing,
   repeated or differing delivery headers do not prevent ingestion/deletion.
4. Configure the shared deny-list redactions secret. Review output before model
   access: deny-list redaction is not complete anonymization.
5. Back up the private original archive and its SQLite ledger together,
   preferably on encrypted storage. Originals are **unredacted, include all
   attachments, and have no automatic expiry**. Never expose the archive through
   OpenCode, `raw-files`, or another public file server.

Sender filtering requires one exact From mailbox if configured. Domains compare
case-insensitively; local parts and plus tags remain exact. Without an allowlist,
headers are not checked before archiving.

Recipient filtering accepts a message when at least one decoded To, Cc or Bcc
mailbox exactly matches `EMAIL_RECIPIENT_ALLOWLIST`. Domains compare
case-insensitively; local parts and plus tags remain exact, so
`test+email@example.com` does not match `test@example.com`. Entries that are not
exact mailboxes (group placeholders, broken addresses) cannot match and never
veto a matching recipient. Delivery headers (`X-Original-To`, `Delivered-To`,
`Envelope-To`, `Received`) are never consulted, and mail delivered without
recipient headers — typically blind-carbon copies — cannot match and stays on the
server. Route BCC-only mail with server-side delivery rules if you need it. Both
allowlists must pass when both are configured; an empty list disables its filter.

The server must advertise **UIDPLUS**. Deletion uses only `UID STORE` for the
matched UID and `UID EXPUNGE <uid>`; never general `EXPUNGE` or `CLOSE`, which could
delete other clients' marked messages. Servers without targeted deletion fail
closed. `BODY.PEEK` leaves the Seen flag unchanged.

## Configuration

In private `.env`:

```env
COMPOSE_PROFILES=email
EMAIL_IMAP_HOST=imap.example.com
EMAIL_IMAP_PORT=993
EMAIL_IMAP_USERNAME=wiki@example.com
EMAIL_IMAP_PASSWORD=replace-with-app-password
EMAIL_IMAP_FOLDER=INBOX
# Optional exact decoded From mailboxes, comma-separated:
EMAIL_FROM_ALLOWLIST=sender@example.com
# Optional exact decoded To/Cc/Bcc mailboxes, comma-separated:
EMAIL_RECIPIENT_ALLOWLIST=test+email@example.com
EMAIL_POLL_INTERVAL=60s
EMAIL_BATCH_SIZE=25
EMAIL_MAX_BYTES=26214400
EMAIL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30
REDACTIONS_FILE=./secrets/redactions.json
```

An empty allowlist disables sender filtering. A configured list applies before
archiving/deletion but is **not authentication**: From is forgeable. Configure
server-side anti-spoofing, SPF/DKIM/DMARC and spam handling. Otherwise spoofed
senders can inject content and incur model costs. Mail is always untrusted data,
never agent instructions. Credentials are provider-only environment variables,
visible to host admins/Docker inspection, not OpenCode. Protect `.env`; use
single-quoted values when necessary to avoid Compose `$` interpolation.

```sh
./karpathy-wiki.sh config --quiet
./karpathy-wiki.sh up -d
```

Changing `.env` requires recreating the service (`up -d` above), not just
restarting it. To pause destructive reception, run
`./karpathy-wiki.sh stop email-ingest`; remove `email` from `COMPOSE_PROFILES`
to keep it disabled on future starts. Stopping cannot undo server deletion;
verified originals remain in the private archive.

**Activation can delete all eligible old mail in the folder.** Non-matching,
oversized or incomplete messages stay on the server. Batches reserve
half their slots (rounded down) for newest UIDs; the remainder advances an
independent rotating backlog cursor. Batch size 1 alternates backlog and newest
turns, persisted across restarts. Growing backlogs and poison/nonmatching messages
cannot monopolize new-mail reception, and older mail continues to be scanned. Limits
default to 25 MiB per original including attachments, 25 candidates per
receive/extraction batch, and 30 seconds per network operation. Polling waits
after a cycle; cycles never overlap. Tests never contact a live mailbox.

## Durability and recovery

`${DATA_ROOT}/incoming/email` is private (`0700`). Immutable `.eml` files (`0600`)
use `YYYY/MM/DD/HH-MM-SS_<id>.eml`, based on the provider's first receipt time
in UTC, never the sender's Date header. The path is stored once and survives
retries, restarts and replay. Names contain no subjects or addresses. Originals
are verified after writing; the file **and parent
directory** are fsynced, then a provider-local SQLite EXTRA-synchronous ledger
commit records the delivery **before** deletion. Disk/state/integrity failures
never permit deletion. A crash before the ledger commit can leave an orphan
original; keep it for operator inspection. Pending deletions resume by
account/folder/UIDVALIDITY/UID with an integrity recheck. Changed UIDVALIDITY
cannot authorize deletion of a reused UID from an old epoch.

Every distinct raw delivery is retained, even if its source exists. Deduplication
uses selected headers and MIME content, excluding transport headers. Identical
copies with differing transit headers share a stable opaque source ID; reused
Message-IDs with changed content remain distinct. Message-ID alone is never a
content identity. Failed deletion does not re-publish a completed source.

**Server deletion follows durable original/ledger storage, not extraction,
redaction or a wiki commit.** Malformed MIME, bad charsets, empty bodies and
privacy failures remain recoverable locally. Extraction errors back off one
hour, stop after five attempts, and remain unhealthy/content-free errors until
repair/replay. An unreachable IMAP server does not prevent local extraction.
No stateless destructive or publication fallback exists.

Pending server deletes recheck the archived message against the current sender
and recipient allowlists as well as archive integrity. MIME identity processing
occurs only after the original is durable; pathological MIME falls back to
exact-original-byte deduplication.
Failed replay retains the last successful projection, subject to the current
privacy gate, and reports the failure without discarding safe published text.

Docker logs record each accepted receipt/archive (original ID and relative path)
and each successful targeted server deletion (original ID), including resumed
deletes. Failures name the operation and exception type only. Logs never include
subjects, addresses, bodies, raw headers or server responses. A successful delete
line is emitted only after the server command and ledger update succeed. These
operational logs are not a replacement for the durable ledger.

Body extraction prefers `text/plain`, otherwise converts HTML locally to text,
preserves signatures/quotes, ignores attachments/embedded messages and loads no
external resources. Markdown uses the decoded Subject as its title (or
`(No subject)`), then From, To, Cc when present, Date including its timezone,
and the body. Bcc, transport/authentication/spam/MIME and provider headers are
omitted. Message-ID and thread references remain available in the private
original, not the Markdown. Attachments stay in the original only; there are no
public attachment links. The complete document crosses the privacy gate;
public IDs/claims are opaque and the whole manifest gets a residual-match check.
Raw addresses, subjects and Message-IDs are never public IDs.

Coherent generations publish through an atomic manifest at
`${DATA_ROOT}/sources/email/manifest.json`, owning wiki subtree `email`. Previous
projections are removed after publication; originals are never pruned. Stricter
redactions recheck/re-redact stored projections on the next cycle; restoring
previously removed values requires replay. Revocations do not erase already
committed wiki knowledge; request cleanup explicitly in the normal wiki workflow.

The canonical original and its redacted Markdown share a date-based directory
and basename; only the extension differs. Publication retains the immutable
generation wrapper, for example:

```text
incoming/email/2026/10/20/18-24-17_<id>.eml
sources/email/generations/<generation>/2026/10/20/18-24-17_<id>.md
```

The first original's opaque ID is also the source ID. Transit-only duplicates
retain their own private originals/paths but share that first source and its
canonical Markdown path. Exact-byte duplicates reuse the archived original.
Raw `.eml` files are never copied into `sources`.

## Explicit offline replay

Stop the daemon before replay; an exclusive archive lock prevents concurrent
receive/replay. Re-extract one source ID from the manifest, or all sources:

```sh
./karpathy-wiki.sh stop email-ingest
./karpathy-wiki.sh run --rm email-ingest email --replay all
# Or: ./karpathy-wiki.sh run --rm email-ingest email --replay <source-id>
./karpathy-wiki.sh up -d email-ingest
```

Replay requires archive/ledger, redactions and publication directory, not IMAP
credentials. It neither contacts nor deletes server mail. Stable IDs keep the
wiki destination; revisions change only when text changes. Algorithm upgrades
never automatically re-extract old originals. Inspect errors and replay after
repair. Use `/ingest-new` for new/changed sources afterward; automatic wiki
ingestion remains disabled. Removing originals sacrifices replay and can block
pending deletes; there is no archive purge command.

# Interactive wiki gap review

Enable the local answer provider with `COMPOSE_PROFILES=answers` (or append
`,answers` to existing profiles). Configure `REDACTIONS_FILE` as for WebDAV,
then restart the stack. The profile is optional; the initial review works
without it. Confirmed drafts can be saved locally without a service-status
check; publication requires the running `answers-ingest` service.

In OpenCode, use `/gap-review` or explicitly ask for an interactive gap review.
The first pass reads the wiki and reports numbered, evidence-linked questions
about missing information, unsupported claims, contradictions, and outdated
syntheses. Reply with answers, skips, or deferrals in the same conversation.
Review the summary and explicitly confirm submission; answering a question
alone does not submit it.

After explicit confirmation, the primary agent immediately saves the Markdown Q&A in
`${DATA_ROOT}/incoming/answers/<unique-name>.md` (mounted at
`/knowledge/incoming/answers` for OpenCode). Each answered question includes
its finding, affected pages, evidence, and attribution to the user. Unanswered
questions and unresolved conflicts remain marked as open. Follow-up requests such
as “ingest the answers” continue this workflow in the primary agent, rather than
dispatching a context-free ingest request. Reader mode cannot save the inbox.
The provider reads
this inbox read-only, applies the configured local redaction rules, and writes
complete source revisions plus a versioned manifest under
`${DATA_ROOT}/sources/answers`. The source tree is read-only to OpenCode;
never copy or edit files there directly. The draft inbox remains private and
is not served by SilverBullet or the raw-files profile. Like other deny-list
redaction, unknown private values can remain; review the sanitized source
before sending it to an external model provider.
When a draft or the redaction rules change, the provider switches the manifest
to the new revision and retires the old published revision; the original stays
only in the private inbox. Published files and the manifest are readable by
the configured instance group, not by other host users.

The agent checks `wiki_ingest_status` for its submitted filename with
`adapter: answers`, `wait_seconds: 60`, and `include_current: true`, allowing
the asynchronous provider to publish before passing
the published source to `wiki-ingest`; only a completed wiki commit and
`current` status count as an imported answer. If publication is delayed or
blocked, check service health, provider logs, and `ANSWERS_SYNC_INTERVAL`, then
retry the status check for the same filename, without writing a duplicate draft
or asking for confirmation again for unchanged answers. The agent reports the
inbox path and distinguishes **saved locally**, **published**, and **imported**.
An absent entry alone does not mean the profile is disabled. Other current
answer sources do not prove that this draft was imported. The ingest handoff
includes the exact source key, revision, and published path; success requires
that revision to be `current` and its commit to be verified. Drafts are retained in
the inbox so restarts and redaction-rule changes can republish them. Do not
delete a submitted draft while it is published: a missing draft makes the
provider unhealthy rather than silently dropping its source. The provider
does not automatically modify the wiki or resolve conflicting claims.

# Ingest modules

Ingest is plugin-based and split into installable Python distributions. The
core repository ships the shared safety core plus two built-in plugins:

```text
ingest/
  core/       karpathy-wiki-ingest            shared core: anonymizer, atomic
              (karpathy_wiki_ingest)          writes, validation, health, plugin
                                              dispatch; ships no plugins
  webdav/     karpathy-wiki-ingest-webdav     rclone sync + generation publisher
              (karpathy_wiki_ingest_webdav)
  audio/      karpathy-wiki-ingest-audio      WebDAV audio snapshots + speech
              (karpathy_wiki_ingest_audio)    handoff + publication
  speech/     karpathy-wiki-speech            speech worker library: timed
              (karpathy_wiki_speech)          segments, faster-whisper and
                                              opt-in hosted backends,
                                              queue/cache between providers
                                              and the worker image
  paperless/  karpathy-wiki-ingest-paperless  Paperless API + sanitizer loop
              (karpathy_wiki_ingest_paperless)
  email/      karpathy-wiki-ingest-email      private IMAP .eml archive + locally
              (karpathy_wiki_ingest_email)    redacted text-only publication/replay
```

Each distribution has its own `pyproject.toml` and is built and installed
independently; the plugin images install the core wheel and exactly one plugin
wheel, so no image ships another plugin's code. The unqualified
`karpathy-wiki-ingest` image is the plugin-free core and serves as the base
image for third-party plugins.

`python -m karpathy_wiki_ingest <plugin>` dispatches to a plugin's `main()`.
Without a plugin name it runs the sole installed plugin (which is what the
per-plugin images rely on); with zero or multiple plugins installed, a name is
required.

## The provider manifest

Every ingest cycle writes a versioned `manifest.json` into its sanitized
source root. It is the end-to-end contract between ingest and the wiki: the
generic `wiki_ingest_status` tool consumes only this manifest and the wiki
pages, and contains no provider-specific code. A manifest lists each
published source with its stable `source_key`, the sanitized `source_path`,
the destination `wiki_path`, the `source_revision`, the exact `frontmatter`
the wiki page must carry, and the `claim` that identifies the source on its
page. Revocations and content-free error reports are part of the manifest.

The name `manifest.json` is reserved at the root of every source directory;
source files with that name are quarantined and never published.

The contract lives in [`contracts/provider-manifest/`](../contracts/provider-manifest/v1/contract.json)
together with shared conformance fixtures that both the Python packages and
the JavaScript scanner tests execute. Sources without a readable, valid
manifest of a supported version are reported as `invalid`; unknown versions
are never silently ignored.

A manifest declares its `wiki_root`: the wiki subtree the provider owns
relative to the wiki source root (`.` for providers that own the whole tree).
Pages are attributed to the manifest with the longest matching `wiki_root`,
so every provider declares its own subtree and `wiki_root` values must be
unique across sources; colliding manifests are reported as `invalid`.

## Adding a module without touching this repository

A module is any Python package that exposes a callable `main()`. It can live
in a separate repo and depends only on the shared core library:

```python
# karpathy_wiki_ingest_mastodon/main.py
from karpathy_wiki_ingest.shared import (
    PrivacyValidationError,
    TargetedAnonymizer,
    atomic_write,
    required_env,
)


def main() -> None: ...
```

Dispatch accepts either of the following; both are discovered automatically,
so a sole installed plugin runs even when it is not named explicitly:

1. **Package convention** - a package named `karpathy_wiki_ingest_<plugin>`
   with a `main()`. This is the recommended path; it needs no extra metadata.
2. **Entry points** - register an entry point named after the plugin in the
   group `karpathy_wiki_ingest.plugins` that points at your `main()`. This is
   what the built-in plugins do.

Build your image on top of the shared core image (it already contains Python,
rclone, and redaction tooling):

```dockerfile
FROM ghcr.io/mstroppel/karpathy-wiki-ingest:${KARPATHY_WIKI_VERSION:-latest}
COPY karpathy_wiki_ingest_mastodon /app/karpathy_wiki_ingest_mastodon
```

Then reference it in `compose.yaml` under an optional profile, mirroring the
built-in services:

```yaml
  mastodon-ingest:
    image: yourrepo/karpathy-wiki-mastodon-ingest:latest
    profiles: ["mastodon"]
```

Because the status scanner reads only the provider manifest, a third-party
module never requires rebuilding the core OpenCode image. A minimal provider
writes sanitized Markdown and one manifest per cycle:

```python
import hashlib
from pathlib import Path

from karpathy_wiki_ingest.manifest import ManifestItem, build_manifest, write_manifest
from karpathy_wiki_ingest.shared import TargetedAnonymizer, atomic_write


def main() -> None:
    incoming = Path("/data/incoming/notes")
    sanitized = Path("/data/sanitized/notes")
    anonymizer = TargetedAnonymizer.from_file(Path("/run/secrets/redactions"))
    items = []
    for source in sorted(incoming.rglob("*.txt")):
        output, _ = anonymizer.anonymize(source.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        revision = hashlib.sha256(output.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
        relative = source.relative_to(incoming).as_posix()
        atomic_write(sanitized / relative, output)
        items.append(
            ManifestItem(
                source_key=relative,
                source_path=relative,
                wiki_path=f"notes/{relative}/index.md",
                source_revision=revision,
                frontmatter={
                    "source_adapter": "notes",
                    "source_path": relative,
                    "source_revision": revision,
                },
                claim={"source_path": relative},
            )
        )
    write_manifest(sanitized / "manifest.json", build_manifest("notes", items, wiki_root="notes"))
```

## Contract versions and deprecation

Both contracts (`karpathy-wiki-ingest-status`, `karpathy-wiki-provider-manifest`)
are versioned documents in `contracts/`. Breaking changes bump the version. A
new manifest version is only introduced together with scanner support, and the
previous version stays readable for one release cycle before removal. Sources
that present an unknown contract or version are reported as `invalid` instead
of being guessed at. Between 1.0.0 releases no compatibility shims are
provided: installations upgrade by re-running ingest and re-importing pages.

## Runtime contract

A module must guarantee the same properties the built-ins provide:

- Read the shared `REDACTIONS_FILE` secret (JSON) and build a
  `TargetedAnonymizer` from it; validate redacted output with `anonymize()` or
  format-aware matching views backed by `locate()`, raising
  `PrivacyValidationError` on residual matches. WebDAV HTML checks literal
  source, decoded entities, and text joined across tags before publication.
- Publish coherent output only. A provider that exposes multiple files for one
  synchronization must build the complete sanitized tree in a private staging
  area and expose it in one atomic publication step, keeping the last
  successful generation active after any failure (the built-in WebDAV plugin
  publishes generations behind an atomic `current` symlink).
- Write only privacy-validated UTF-8 source text (Markdown or HTML) to
  `SANITIZED_ROOT`, non-destructively via
  `atomic_write()`; files that fail text decoding or privacy validation go to
  `QUARANTINE_ROOT` as content-free error reports and are removed from the
  candidate sanitized tree. HTML retains active content and must be treated as
  untrusted source text, not safe-to-render pages; redaction is not HTML
  sanitization.
- Operate under `PUID:PGID`, honor a `--once` flag for one-shot runs, and
  tolerate concurrent wiki reads during writes.
- Keep the source layout and front matter format versioned; OpenCode and the
  ingest skill read the contracts, not the plugin code. The versioned status
  contract with shared conformance fixtures lives in
  [`contracts/ingest-status/`](../contracts/ingest-status/v1/contract.json),
  and the provider manifest contract in
  [`contracts/provider-manifest/`](../contracts/provider-manifest/v1/contract.json);
  both the Python packages and the JavaScript status scanner are tested
  against the same fixtures. Every cycle must end by writing a valid
  `manifest.json` into the sanitized source root.

The core image provides the environment; a module must not require extra
services reachable from the wiki network. Attach any needed network
explicitly in Compose.

# Wiki ingestion

`/ingest-new` starts `wiki_ingest_batch` once. Code snapshots the accepted pending
selection and processes it sequentially, with one commit per source.
`/ingest <source>` uses an exact source-path filter. Already-current sources are
not reinterpreted. Later arrivals wait for another explicit request. No scheduler,
background controller or per-source repository clone is introduced.

## Private per-source attempts

Each source gets one fresh child session and one private draft under
`incoming/ingest-journal/drafts/<batch>/<attempt>/wiki`. It contains the selected
source page and shared editable Markdown context, index/log and safety instructions,
not other source pages, Git history or configuration. Workers can read targeted
live wiki context but cannot write it. Read-only sources stay under `/knowledge/sources`.
For other source pages, workers read `/knowledge/wiki/sources/<wiki-path>` directly;
their absence in the draft is expected, not evidence of a missing live page.
Code alone owns frontmatter, index/log and publication. The initializer never
replaces existing `AGENTS.md`; manually align ingest task ownership and the private
draft exception while preserving all local safety rules.

Admission binds child, parent, exact source/target, draft and running Linux process
incarnation in private short-lived records. Prompt data or stale records grant no
admission. Workers cannot read other drafts/control files or change source material.
Directory reads of the draft root and live wiki root are allowed; write permissions
are not broadened.

Worker task data uses `wiki_root: .` and a relative `wiki_path`; absolute draft
roots stay internal to batch code. Draft reads and mutations (including every
patch file header) require relative paths resolving inside the assigned draft.
An assignment-scoped tool preflight rejects violations with `ingest_path_contract`
before native execution. Absolute reads remain available for the exact assigned
original source, live wiki context and ingest skill files, subject to existing
permissions. Header extraction respects native add/update body boundaries;
header-looking update context is not a target or source-write evidence. Native
tools still validate complete patch syntax. This is fail-fast validation, not
typo correction or a guarantee against model mistakes: path-contract failures
remain fatal even after a later successful call. No paths are guessed, rewritten
or retried and no permissions
are broadened.

Completion requires native evidence: fully covered source reads, successful skill
loading and an explicit mutation of the exact selected page, plus valid final files,
unchanged source identity/digest, permitted diff and a verified commit. Session
success or prose alone is insufficient. Rewriting unchanged supported findings is
allowed. Corrected exact missing-target reads, mandatory reads/skills and safe
patch corrections remain auditable; explicit permission rejections are never
forgiven. Pagination must cover the complete source. For the exact assigned source,
`read` returns lossless, JSON-quoted segments with original line numbers and
zero-based Unicode code-point ranges. Each page contains at most 4,000 source
characters and 64 segments; a segment contains at most 1,000 characters. Follow
the byte-bounded pages (at most 12,000 rendered UTF-8 bytes, including continuation)
even when quoting or multibyte text lowers the character count. Use
the returned `Continue read` arguments (`offset`, `character_offset`, `limit`)
until `End of source`. Code-owned tool metadata and matching delivered text
certify a line only when its segments cover every character without gaps. Duplicate or overlapping reads do
not fill missing ranges. Ignored continuations remain `worker_source_truncated`;
native long-line truncation also never certifies unseen text.

Original line terminators belong to their line's quoted text and character range,
including CRLF and final newlines. The publication line count uses this same
untrimmed representation, so trailing whitespace-only lines also require delivery.
Equivalent admitted paths resolve to the same assigned source and use the same
segment reader. Native numbered-line text without segment receipts never proves
source completeness.

Native read permission/path checks run before the source is read through the
existing regular-file, no-link, UTF-8 and 8 MiB boundaries. Source bytes, revisions
and line references are unchanged. Other files and sessions retain native paging;
`character_offset` is available only for the admitted source. This is transport
paging within one worker, not semantic splitting, summarization or another attempt.

There is no application context-budget planner, semantic source chunker, rollover, automatic
repair or source retry. OpenCode V2 has no worker-scoped compaction setting; the
worker compaction hook stops the attempt before a summary request, using the native
boundary rather than another token estimate. This can occur before the provider's
hard context window. Other chats retain normal compaction. A provider context
overflow also leaves that source unpublished. The report explains that source,
wiki context and tool output together reached the model window, and suggests
splitting/preprocessing the source or choosing a larger-context model. A renewed
attempt requires an explicit new request, not routine per-source approval questions.

Independent sources continue after isolated failures, including post-write failures
and context limits. Provider/configuration failures, exhausted storage or foreign
wiki changes stop new dispatch. Native transient provider retries are bounded to
three attempts; no application-level retry loop or model-call/deadline budget is
added. OCR gaps and contradictions are reported, not automatic rejection reasons.

Defaults reserve 32 MiB per draft, limit files to 8 MiB and retained attempts to
256 MiB/16,384 entries. Unchanged copies in failed attempts are reclaimed; changed
or uncertain evidence is retained and never reused. Successful drafts are removed
only after durable publication. A cleanup failure reports `draft_cleanup_failed`
and stops new dispatch without downgrading the verified commit; already-absent
completed drafts are harmless. Capacity exhaustion never silently deletes evidence.
Back up the journal and wiki `.git`; existing retention policy applies.

## Results and interruption

`done` means the accepted selection completed; `partial` means sources failed or
metadata diagnostics remain; `blocked` means a shared technical blocker;
`cancelled` means interrupted. Counts and fresh status expose remaining, invalid
and conflicting sources separately. No automatic reconciliation of historical
live leftovers is performed. Dirty admission preserves edits and stops before
workers start; cleanup requires separate inspection and authorization.

Failed private work closes with a report, not an active recovery conversation.
A new explicit request selects pending sources afresh, never reuses an old draft
or approval. After process death during private work, the next entry closes that
interrupted batch without model work; another explicit request starts new work.

## Durable publication and reports

Every completed call returns a per-source brief for up to ten selected sources
in `sources`, with `sources_total` and `sources_omitted`. Chat always shows each
returned source's readable filename or email subject/date, short title, publication
status, and one to five sentences about changes and relevant uncertainties. For
larger batches it explicitly counts the additional entries in the private report;
it does not silently omit them. The serialized brief list is also capped at 12 KiB
(including multibyte prose and changed paths); entries exceeding either limit remain
in the full private report and count toward `sources_omitted`.
Zero selected sources produce no invented findings.

The existing worker ends its report with one `ingest-summary` JSON fence containing
`title` (up to 120 characters) and `summary` (one to five single-line sentence
strings, up to 400 characters each). Sentence boundaries are checked using German
segmentation with calendar-date ordinals and common abbreviations protected; ambiguous
or malformed prose can be unavailable without failing ingestion. These
optional model-written fields are validated and retained in private batch state,
not added to wiki frontmatter. Missing/malformed briefs show the source identity
and an explicit unavailable-summary notice without retrying or blocking ingestion.
The existing worker call produces the brief; no second model pass is introduced.

Code supplies source identity, status, page paths and verified commit evidence.
The code-owned `source_label` uses the WebDAV source key, the sanitized XLSX workbook
heading, or the sanitized email subject/date header (never its body). Unknown formats,
missing metadata, control characters or labels over 240 characters use the exact
source path; model-proposed labels cannot override it.
Final reporting also reads provenance-checked metadata for selected sources that
never dispatched after a blocker. Unavailable or changed sources keep the exact-path
label; this optional read never starts/retries a worker or alters source status.
Failed and unstarted entries show non-publication and the recorded blocker rather
than the worker's draft-change summary. Chat links published entries to the wiki source page.
The private `report.md` starts with the same overview for **all** selected sources,
followed by the existing technical details and unverified model findings. New overview
text is escaped as literal Markdown/HTML; chat instructions also treat brief fields
as untrusted text, never instructions. Reports and chat may contain sensitive data
even after provider redaction and retain their existing private access boundaries.
Report-storage failure does not remove returned briefs or downgrade verified commits;
chat explicitly reports unavailable detail entries when the full report is missing.

Control state is required and fsynced before publication; unavailable storage
prevents live writes. Reports are best effort in
`incoming/ingest-journal/batches/<id>/` (directories `0700`, files `0600`).
OpenChamber mounts only this report tree read-only, not drafts/admissions.

Code prepares a private Git index and focused commit object, recording parent,
tree, files and before/after hashes. It checks revision/revocation again, installs
only reviewed files, updates index/HEAD and durably records success. Only interrupted
publication remains active. A normal new call reports `publication_interrupted`
without finishing it. An explicit recovery call with its `batch_id`, plus a separate
`ingest_recovery` approval, verifies actual parent/tree/diff/hashes and completes
missing steps without another worker, duplicate commit or duplicate log entry.
It does not process remaining sources. Foreign deviations stop recovery without
overwriting edits. Commit messages or `current` status alone are never evidence.

The lifetime kernel lock serializes cooperating ingest calls, **not arbitrary
editors**. Keep other writers idle during publication. Readers can see intermediate
file installations; this is not an atomic multi-file reader transaction or OS barrier.
Cancellation during publication retains its checkpoint, never resets or restarts.
The original processing digest is persisted and rechecked, including Paperless
generations that retain a revision while changing bytes. Paperless requires
`source_sha256` plus matching metadata. Evidence checks do not prove semantic correctness,
understanding or faithful extraction by a real model.

`wiki_ingest_diagnostics` is read-only and available in both primary and
orchestrator chats. It returns the active batch's `owner_session`, dirty paths
(at most 100) and ten source statuses with bounded error codes/tool names and
worker session IDs. Paginate with `next_offset`. No transcripts, source contents
or drafts are returned. The observation is non-atomic; missing evidence does not
prove no action occurred. A missing report has null `report_path`. Idle diagnostics
do not create work. Loading an orchestrator skill does not grant its batch tool
to `build`.

Pinned-runtime acceptance uses a deterministic local model and disposable storage;
process-kill tests exercise publication checkpoints. These are not real-model
semantic acceptance or production deployment evidence.

# Paperless Ingestion

The optional importer selects Paperless-ngx documents by tag, reads OCR text and
selected metadata, replaces explicitly configured personal values locally, and
writes only sanitized Markdown into `/knowledge/sources/paperless`.

It does not download PDFs or images. It does not use an external redaction
service. Unknown personal values, unexpected spelling, and OCR variants may
remain, so this process must not be treated as guaranteed anonymization.

## Setup

1. Create a dedicated Paperless user with read access only to the selected
   documents.
2. Create a source tag and determine its positive numeric ID through the
   Paperless API.
3. Create an API token for the dedicated user.
4. Copy `redactions.example.json` to a private location and enter every known
   value and variant that must be replaced.
5. Store the token without a trailing newline and protect both files with mode
   `0600`.
6. Enable the profile and generated policy:

```env
COMPOSE_PROFILES=webdav,paperless
PAPERLESS_PUBLIC_URL=https://paperless.example.com
PAPERLESS_SOURCE_TAG_ID=123
PAPERLESS_TOKEN_FILE=/private/wiki/paperless-token
REDACTIONS_FILE=/private/wiki/redactions.json
```

Run a one-off synchronization before enabling continuous polling:

```bash
docker compose --profile paperless run --rm paperless-ingest paperless --once
```

Inspect sanitized output and the content-free error reports under
`${DATA_ROOT}/quarantine/paperless` locally. Do not send test documents to a
model provider until the review is complete.

## Revision Model

Published files contain `paperless_id`, `paperless_url`, and a deterministic
`source_revision`. The revision hashes the sanitized rendered document with a
fixed empty revision field, avoiding a self-referential hash. Only changes to
the published content or metadata (including redaction counts and the original
link) produce a new revision; an unrelated redaction rule does not. The separate
`source_sha256` hashes all final published bytes for integrity verification.
Documents are split into ID ranges of no more than 1000 items.

Each synchronization builds all sanitized documents and revocations in a new
private generation. The provider manifest points at the files under
`sources/paperless/generations/<id>/` rather than a mutable source path.
An atomic `current` symlink selects the active generation; the manifest is
replaced only after the complete generation is available. Failed fetches,
decoding, or writes leave the previous generation and manifest active.
Privacy validation failures are recorded as content-free errors and any
previously published copy is revoked in the new generation. The redaction file
is reloaded on each daemon cycle. Unchanged cycles retain the existing
generation; completed replacements retain only the active generation.
The shared redaction fingerprint includes a code-maintained algorithm version,
so bumping that version for a behavior-changing redaction update reprocesses
selected documents on the next cycle without editing `redactions.json`. This
is shared with WebDAV, so a bump invalidates both current redaction-enabled
sources.

A rule or algorithm-version change still checks every selected original locally,
including when a rule is removed. Private input hashes include the redaction
fingerprint for durable jobs and snapshot validation; they are separate from
published document revisions. A replacement generation can therefore have new
file paths but unchanged document revisions. `/ingest-new` processes only new or
changed revisions, not sources whose generation path alone changed.

After an interrupted cycle, the next run removes abandoned `.staging-*`
directories. If the active pointer or manifest is corrupt, stop the importer,
inspect `current` and `manifest.json`, and restore a consistent pair from a
backup rather than changing individual files. The file `.generation.json`
contains only a redaction fingerprint, source revision hashes, the digest of
the manifest written for the generation, the source tag ID, and the configured
public URL; it does not contain source text or tokens.

**Existing pre-1.0 flat Paperless installations:** back up `DATA_ROOT`, stop the
Paperless service, and manually remove the old flat sanitized source files,
`revoked.md`, and `manifest.json` under `sources/paperless` before starting this
layout. The next cycle fetches and republishes the selected documents. Review
any previous revocations and wiki pages before re-importing. The importer
refuses a flat layout instead of silently mixing generations with old files.

### Durable cycles

With the Compose-provided `INGEST_STATE_PATH`, Paperless identifies each cycle
by the selected documents' revisions, the redaction fingerprint, source tag,
and public URL. It records a content-free accepted job in the shared SQLite
store before publishing. A lease with periodic renewal fences a worker that
loses authority; failed work backs off, and an unchanged failed input becomes
dead after repeated attempts. A restart checks the active manifest and
generation before retrying, so a cycle that published before its job completed
is recorded without a duplicate generation. A changed upstream snapshot
supersedes older pending jobs. Raw API documents are kept only in memory and
are never persisted in job payloads or health metrics.

The daemon's health record includes the shared store's queue depth, age,
failed/retried counts, last recorded source generation, and last committed
wiki publication. An unavailable or incompatible state store stops the
Paperless cycle instead of publishing without coordination.

The `paperless_url` frontmatter field is validated HTTPS and repeated as
trusted page frontmatter in the provider manifest, so every generated wiki
summary page can render a visible link to the Paperless original; the
`wiki-ingest` skill preserves the field and the link, and `wiki-lint` reports
Paperless pages that lose it.

Removing the source tag omits the document from the new generation and records
the ID in `current/revoked.md`. Existing derived wiki knowledge is reported but not automatically
deleted because it may be supported by additional sources.

After every cycle the plugin writes the provider manifest
`sources/paperless/manifest.json` describing the published documents, their
revisions, their wiki destinations, and any content-free errors.

Use `/ingest-new` in OpenCode to compare source revisions with existing wiki
pages and process new or changed documents sequentially.

## Network Boundary

Only `paperless-ingest` requires Paperless API access. Ensure the importer can
reach the Paperless-ngx API over the network it shares; do not attach OpenCode
to that network. OpenCode's policy also prohibits direct API access, and
`PAPERLESS_BLOCKED_HOSTNAME` maps the configured public hostname to loopback.
These application controls remain defense in depth rather than a replacement
for network isolation.

# Runtime write isolation

`WIKI_RUNTIME_READ_ONLY=true` opts into a **reader-only OpenCode runtime**.
It is an independent kernel-enforced read-only mode, not writer serialization
or automatic ingestion.

## Enable

Set this in the installation's `.env`, then recreate OpenCode:

```env
WIKI_RUNTIME_READ_ONLY=true
```

```sh
./karpathy-wiki.sh up -d --force-recreate opencode
```

Compose mounts wiki, sources, the **entire** private ingest-journal and confirmed
answer inbox read-only. The container root is also read-only. Runtime credentials,
sessions, settings and state retain their separate writable mounts. Temporary
storage and the runtime cache are ephemeral. `/tmp` allows execution because the
pinned Bun runtime extracts its PTY native library there; this does not grant
write access to protected mounts or extra capabilities.

The shipped entrypoint checks the actual kernel mount table and filesystem flags
before launching OpenCode. It refuses root execution, nonzero capability sets,
missing `no-new-privileges`, a writable root/protected mount, writable overlapping
submounts, writable aliases of protected backing paths or an exposed default
Docker socket. Unsafe topology produces only a content-free startup error.
No model instructions, permission hook, API path filter or backend password is
the enforcement mechanism: all processes start without protected write access.

Default `false` preserves manual authoring. Return to that mode by setting
`false` and recreating the container. A restart alone does not apply changed
Compose mounts. This changes no stored data layout and performs no migration.

## Supported behavior and boundary

In reader mode, model questions, file reads and private session state remain
available. Direct `/ingest-new`, `/analysis-save`, journal/report writes and
saving confirmed `/gap-review` answers are denied. There is no alternate
publication channel. The ingest lock is unavailable on read-only storage;
that does not imply another active writer.

Authenticated API/configuration access is **not** sandboxed in general. Runtime
secrets and sessions remain within the backend's existing authority. The guarantee
is no mutation of the protected backing trees by this unprivileged runtime,
including direct APIs, plugins, spawned shells and PTYs. It is not protection
against kernel/container-runtime exploits or an administrator who changes the
deployment, grants a remote writer credential, exposes a privileged socket or
pre-seeds writable hardlink aliases outside the protected trees. Keep host data
roots disjoint and do not expose Docker/host-writer authority to OpenCode.
Initialization and source providers are separate trusted
writers outside this runtime boundary; do not mistake reader mode for their
coordination or for immutable source publication over time.

## Pinned-image proof

```sh
docker build --target opencode -t kw-opencode:integration -f opencode/Dockerfile .
sh tests/integration/runtime-write-isolation.sh
```

The runner uses disposable named volumes, no host data, no exposed ports, no
external network and no model calls. It checks both rendered Compose modes,
confirms a direct API write succeeds in manual mode, and then runs the isolated
mode with the pinned OpenCode API. It verifies:

- Direct writes from wiki and unrelated locations cannot overwrite/create files.
- Actual location/session shells and a PTY execute overwrite/create/unlink/rename,
  chmod, mkdir and symlink attempts: the kernel returns `EROFS`.
- Symlink and `/proc/self/root` paths, hardlink escape and remount cannot bypass it.
- The actual report writer cannot write; the ingest lock syscall returns
  `EROFS` and its core refuses admission. A synthetic custom command invokes these
  cores without asking a model; this is not model-facing tool-dispatch validation.
- Runtime/configuration writes outside the protected trees remain possible but
  do not restore protected write access. Entire protected tree contents, entries,
  permissions and ownership are unchanged, including Git and journal evidence.
- The same checks pass after restart, and startup rejects a writable backing
  alias or a read-only flag paired with writable mounts.

CI runs this positive boundary proof. It does not make writable mode safe for
concurrent writers or implement the deferred automatic-ingest feature (#157).

# Excel tables through WebDAV

Enable and configure the existing `webdav` profile and `REDACTIONS_FILE` as
described in [configuration](configuration.md#secrets). Upload an unencrypted
`.xlsx` to `WEBDAV_PATH`, alongside ordinary Markdown/HTML sources. **Never put
files directly in `sources/webdav`.** Originals remain in private
`incoming/webdav`; only the locally extracted, redacted Markdown is published.
Then use normal manual wiki ingest (`/ingest-new` or an explicitly selected
source). This does not schedule wiki ingest or introduce another service.

## Extracted content

- Workbook identity (relative upload path), worksheet names, headers and cell
  values are retained. Tables use Excel column letters and row numbers; each
  sheet records its bounding range. Interior blank cells/rows stay in position;
  empty outer ranges and formatting-only cells are omitted.
- Only visible worksheets, rows and columns are included. Hidden/very-hidden
  sheets, hidden rows/columns (including grouped columns), comments, document
  properties, charts, images and hyperlink targets are omitted. Merged ranges
  are listed explicitly: only the anchor carries a value; other merged cells
  are marked, not populated with duplicated values. A hidden anchor is not
  copied to visible cells. Every extract states these omissions.
- Numbers, booleans, Excel errors, ISO dates/times and durations are labelled.
  Numeric formats `General`, `0`, `#,##0`, up to six decimal zeroes, a trailing
  `%`, or a trailing quoted unit (e.g. `0.00 "kg"`) are supported. Group separators
  are normalized away. Other numeric formats keep the underlying number with an
  explicit **unsupported number format** annotation. Currency/accounting,
  conditional/locale-specific formats and Excel's visual layout are not rendered.
  Dates/times are semantic ISO values, not a reproduction of their Excel display.
- Default-hidden sheet row/column layouts are rejected rather than guessing
  visibility. Malformed or overlapping column definitions are also rejected:
  copy the visible data to a fresh worksheet before uploading.
- Formula cells include their expressions as calculation context and cached
  results with the same type labels. **No formulas are calculated or verified.**
  A missing cache is marked `MISSING cached result`, never replaced by zero;
  Excel errors such as `#DIV/0!` are explicit. Simple formula strings are supported;
  array/data-table formula objects are rejected rather than silently omitted.
  Visible expressions may still name hidden sheets/ranges, and cached results
  may derive from hidden cells: hidden content is not extracted directly.

**Before uploading: open the workbook in Excel, recalculate, then save it.**
Other writers (including openpyxl) may omit formula caches. A cache can still be
stale; the provider cannot establish freshness or correctness.

## Privacy and safety

All included workbook-derived text, including upload identity, sheet names,
number-format annotations, formulas and cached strings, crosses the shared local
deny-list redactor **before** Markdown/HTML escaping. Unknown sensitive values may
remain: inspect the sanitized extract before sending it to a model.

No macros execute and no external links, entities or data connections are fetched.
Legacy `.xls`, `.xlsb` and macro-enabled `.xlsm` are excluded from synchronization;
use an unencrypted `.xlsx` instead. If already present locally, these unsupported
formats are still rejected with export instructions. Encrypted, corrupt or
unsupported packages produce fixed actionable diagnostics, without workbook text
or raw parser errors.
Other non-source formats remain ignored. rclone output is suppressed because its
diagnostics can contain private filenames; sync failures remain visible in health.

Each workbook runs in its own parser subprocess with these fixed limits:

| Resource | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Compressed input | 20 MiB |
| Total uncompressed ZIP members | 100 MiB |
| ZIP members / XML elements | 2,048 / 1,000,000 |
| Compression ratio for members over 1 MiB | 200:1 |
| Worksheets (including hidden) | 32 |
| Row / column coordinates | 10,000 / 256 |
| Examined row records across workbook | 50,000 |
| Examined cell records / total output bounding rectangles | 200,000 each |
| Merged ranges across workbook | 2,000; each at most 200,000 cells |
| Parser memory / CPU / wall time | 768 MiB / 30 seconds / 45 seconds |
| Private parser result / final UTF-8 Markdown | 4 MiB each |

Limits include hidden content when examining input. Oversized/suspicious workbooks
fail explicitly; there is no successful truncated extract. Split or simplify the
workbook and re-upload. Private quarantine reports use a path hash and a fixed
diagnostic. Any extraction/redaction failure retains the entire last successful
source generation and its manifest, including the previously published workbook;
it does not publish the other files from the failed cycle either.

## Identity, updates and provenance

An XLSX uploaded at relative path `P` publishes to
`generations/<id>/xlsx/<sha256(P UTF-8)>/workbook.md`. Its source key is
`xlsx/<hash>/workbook.md`, with wiki target `webdav/<source-key>/index.md` under
the normal `sources/` wiki subtree. Manifest claims and frontmatter contain the
opaque stable key, never the raw filename. Generation inventory uses the same
path hash; the sanitized heading carries the redacted human-readable identity.

Ordinary Markdown/HTML retain their paths; `table.xlsx` and `table.xlsx.md`
coexist. If an ordinary file deliberately occupies a hashed workbook output
path (or an ancestor/descendant), the cycle fails closed; rename that conflicting
upload. No source can overwrite another output.

Edits and deletions use the existing generation/manifest contract. Revisions are
SHA-256 hashes of sanitized Markdown, so unchanged output keeps the same revision
and claim. Redaction changes regenerate extracts. The code-maintained
`EXTRACTION_VERSION` in `ingest/webdav/src/karpathy_wiki_ingest_webdav/xlsx.py`
also participates in cycle identity/metadata; bump it for extraction, rendering,
dependency or limit changes. There is no change to the manual wiki provenance
contract.

suggest creating them upfront. `/domain-modeling`, reached through

when terms or decisions are resolved.

Continue following `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `README.md`, and the existing

- `GLOSSARY.md`: shared domain vocabulary.

# Issue tracker: GitHub

Issues and specs live in GitHub Issues for `mstroppel/karpathy-wiki`.
Use the `gh` CLI for all operations. Infer the repository from the Git
remote; `gh` does this automatically inside a clone.

## Conventions

- Create: `gh issue create --title "..." --body-file <file>`.
  Use a heredoc or body file for multi-line bodies.
- Read: `gh issue view <number> --comments`; fetch labels with
  `gh issue view <number> --json labels`.
- List: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments`.
  Apply appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.
- Comment: `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`.
- Apply or remove labels: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label "..."`
  or `--remove-label "..."`.
- Close: `gh issue close <number> --comment "..."`.

Follow `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `SECURITY.md`: never publish private source
material, credentials, redaction values, or other sensitive data.

## Pull requests as a triage surface

**PRs as a request surface: no.**

GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs. Resolve ambiguous
references with `gh pr view <number>`, falling back to `gh issue view <number>`.

## Skill instructions

- “Publish to the issue tracker”: create a GitHub issue.
- “Fetch the relevant ticket”: run `gh issue view <number> --comments`.

## Wayfinding operations

- Map: one issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding Notes, Decisions-so-far,
  and Fog.
- Child ticket: link as a GitHub sub-issue using `gh api`. If sub-issues
  are unavailable, use a task list in the map and `Part of #<map>` in the
  child. Label `wayfinder:<type>`: research, prototype, grilling, or task.
- Blocking: use native issue dependencies:
  `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`.
  Obtain the database ID with
  `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<number> --jq .id`.
  If unavailable, record `Blocked by: #<number>` in the child.
- Frontier: list open children in map order; exclude assigned tickets
  and tickets with open blockers.
- Claim: `gh issue edit <number> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.
- Resolve: comment with the result, close the child, and append a context
  pointer to the map's Decisions-so-far. Do not publish sensitive data.

# Diagramme speichern

Nur für fertige Analysen mit mitgelieferten Diagrammen; keine neue Analyse oder
Werte erfinden. Grafikdateien sind genauso wie Markdown veröffentlichter Inhalt.

1. Speichere PNG oder statische SVG unter `assets/analyses/<slug>/<name>.png`
   beziehungsweise `.svg`. Namen: ASCII-Kebab-Case, keine Unterverzeichnisse.
2. Binde sie als `![Aussagekräftiger Alternativtext](/.fs/assets/analyses/<slug>/<name>.svg)`
   ein. Kein HTML, Inline-SVG, externer Bildabruf oder vorgefertigte Data-URL.
3. PNG muss statisch und dekodierbar sein. SVG braucht den Namespace
   `http://www.w3.org/2000/svg`; ein optionaler `viewBox` muss positive Breite
   und Höhe haben. Unterstützt werden
   Formen, Pfade, Gruppen, Text, lokale Ausschnitte, Schraffuren, Gradienten,
   Marker und lokale `use`-Referenzen. Verwende Darstellungsattribute oder einfache
   `style`-Deklarationen, keine Stylesheets, Metadaten-Namespaces, Fremdbilder,
   Skripte, Animationen oder externen Ressourcen. Referenzen dürfen nur auf IDs
   derselben SVG zeigen. Nicht unterstützte Konstrukte sind ein Fehler; entferne
   keine bedeutungstragenden Diagrammteile als stillen Ersatz.
4. Beachte Grenzen: PNG 10 MiB/40 Megapixel, SVG 2 MiB/10.000 Elemente,
   maximal 50 Bildeinbindungen und 50 MiB fertiges HTML. SVG-Dimensionen sind
   ebenfalls begrenzt; der Renderer nennt verletzte Struktur-/Wertregeln.
5. Führe `render-analysis` aus. Prüfe die gemeldete PNG-/SVG-Anzahl, sichtbare
   Diagramme und lesbare Werte/Quellen. Erhalte eine zugängliche Datentabelle,
   wenn sie Teil der Analyse ist. Keine erfundene Interaktivität behaupten:
   eingebettete Diagramme sind statische Bilder.
6. Committe Diagrammassets zusammen mit Analyse und HTML. Bei einem Renderfehler
   bleibt eine vorherige Druckansicht erhalten, ist aber kein aktueller Erfolg.
